reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E1 describes differential diffusion in a Cantor alloy but notes no protective Cr2O3 formed, contradicting the premise of a protective Cr-rich scale. E2 mentions CrTaO4 and Al2O3 in a specific RHEA but does not address grain-boundary effects or controlled diffusion. E3 shows Al content can change oxidation kinetics in a different alloy system but does not link this to grain-boundary-mediated diffusion. The premises about microstructural refinement and synergistic diffusion remain unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Al and Cr have inherently lower diffusivities in HEAs, allowing them to accumulate at the surface
A refined microstructure (increased grain-boundary density) accelerates selective transportation of Al and Cr to the surface
The resulting duplex oxide scale (e.g., Cr-rich outer with internal Al2O3 or CrTaO4) acts as an effective oxygen diffusion barrier
Optimizing Al/Cr content and refining grain structure leads to a more continuous, adherent protective oxide scale
This mechanism yields lower mass gains and slower parabolic oxidation kinetics compared to a coarse-grained, non-optimized baseline
